tools.name: get_content_queue
tools.description: Get the queue of draft posts waiting to be published or scheduled, with each draft's text, intended action (publish / schedule), and any target date.

tools.name: get_following

tools.name: get_events

user_tasks.prompt: Work through these independent moderation/engagement streams. The target of every action is NOT given to you directly — you must inspect the account's hidden state (posts, comments, DMs, mentions, followers) to resolve it first. The streams do not depend on each other, so any order is fine. Stream 1: find the post that has drawn the most reports and delete it. Stream 2: read your DMs, find whoever asked you for the meetup slides, and reply to them. Stream 3: read your follower list, find your only verified follower, and follow them back.

subtasks.label: delete the most-reported post
reply to the follower who asked for the slides
follow back the only verified follower

user_tasks.prompt: Independent back-office jobs — for EACH, inspect the relevant records to find the details, then carry out ALL its steps. (1) directory: apply the pending account & contacts updates (a moved contact's new handle, and the queued bio and contact-email changes). (2) outreach: DM each of my key campaign contacts at the handle currently on file for them in the contacts registry. (3) moderation: enforce safety on the flagged content — delete the phishing comment, block the account behind the harassment mention, and report the spam commenter. (4) network: tidy up the follow graph — follow back my only verified follower, unfollow the account that has gone inactive, and mute the noisy one. (5) content: clear the content queue — publish the draft marked for publishing and schedule the one marked for scheduling at its target date — and delete the post that has drawn the most reports. IMPORTANT — ordering & fresh lookups: FIRST complete the records/registry maintenance step; THEN, for every send/pay/act step, resolve each recipient/target/destination from the CURRENT on-file registry AT THE MOMENT you act (the records may have just been updated) — do not reuse a value you read earlier, and never assume a hard-coded destination.
